scenario: AITA: My friend sent me a screenshot of her grades, and I'm upset | The other day my friend texted me: "\[cramberrycat\], look, isn't it beautiful?" and sent me a screenshot of her grades: a column of straight A's. It was only this narrow strip, which means she must've taken the pains to crop the screenshot so only the grade letters showed up: no class names, percentages, or extra stuff. ​ I forgot exactly what I did. I know I was kind of surprised and irritated that she did this. (Who sends their friends screenshots of their grades? Is this a thing? If so, please fill me in.) Granted, we are on the nerdier side of friends and of course we talk about grades, but I felt like this was too much. I might've ignored her text for a few hours because I was afraid I might say something wrong, which would probably mark me as the A-hole, but I can't remember if I did. ​ Some time after she had already sent the screenshot, she texted me "Sorry" so I'm not sure, maybe she realized how I might feel and apologized for crossing some sort of line? (If there is, in fact, such a line?) I eventually replied, "Truly a sight to behold", which was deliberate in that it did not reflect my true feelings at all. ​ But in terms of my feelings, and my non-verbal reaction, AITA? Was I wrong to be so upset by it? I just felt it was kind of annoying and unnecessary. I'm not sure if she did it with the intention of hurting me or making me jealous; I'm less open about my grades than she is, because she gets consistent high A's on tests while I get B+'s to low A's, although formerly I was a high A's student. I just feel like I'm being too sensitive or overanalyzing it, which has been the case many a time in the past.

message.reasoning: Okay, so I'm trying to figure out whether I was wrong to be upset when my friend sent me a screenshot of her grades. Let me start by understanding the situation better. My friend sent me a screenshot of her grades, which were all straight A's. She cropped it so that only the grades showed, no class names or percentages. I was surprised and irritated because I don't think people usually send their grades to friends. I felt like it was too much, and I ignored her texts for a few hours because I was worried about saying the wrong thing. Later, she apologized, and I replied with "Truly a sight to behold," which didn't reflect my true feelings. Now, I'm wondering if I was being too sensitive or overreacting. First, I need to consider why she sent the screenshot. Maybe she was proud of her grades and wanted to share them. But she cropped it so that only the grades showed, which might mean she wanted to highlight her achievements without giving too much detail. On the other hand, maybe she intended to show off her grades, which could make others feel inferior, especially if they have lower grades. I also need to think about how I felt when I saw the screenshot. I was surprised and irritated, which suggests that it was unexpected and made me uncomfortable. I ignored her texts, which might have made her feel bad, especially since she later apologized. My response of "Truly a sight to behold" was sarcastic and didn't convey my true feelings, which might have been hurtful or confusing for her. Another thing to consider is our friendship. We are on the nerdier side and talk about grades, but does that mean it's okay to send screenshots of grades? I don't think so. Grades are personal, and sharing them publicly or even privately can be sensitive. It's possible that she didn't realize how it would make me feel, especially since I'm less open about my grades and have lower grades than her. I also need to reflect on whether I was overreacting. Maybe I was being too sensitive because I'm insecure about my own grades. It's possible that her intention wasn't to make me jealous or upset, but rather to share her success. However, the way she presented it, by cropping only the grades, might have come off as boastful or insensitive. In the end, I think it's important to communicate my feelings to her instead of ignoring her or responding sarcastically. That way, she can understand how her actions affected me, and we can work on our friendship moving forward.
